subject: Throughput & Spend Alignment — monthly tokens and burst TPS
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Kira Mitchell <kira@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: throughput & spend alignment — quick clarifying items

Hi Kira — great to meet today, thanks for the demo time. Quick recap + a few asks so we can size a hosted API proposal that matches Atlas Health's expected economics.

Call takeaways (brief):
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant for patient intake and care-routing (mix of short prompts + ~400 token expected completions).
- Target go-live: Q3 pilot, ramp through Q4.
- Key success criteria: predictable spend, <100ms median token latency, graceful handling of bursts.

Items I need from you to finalize a pricing sketch:
1) Monthly token volume (range is fine) — e.g., baseline vs peak month.
2) Typical and peak TPS sustained/burst numbers (how many requests per second at peak).
3) Target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range so we can align tiers.
4) Any hard constraints (SLA, PII residency) that would change hosting mode.

Attached is a short worksheet (redwood-hosted-pricing-worksheet.xlsx) that shows example unit economics at different slab sizes — fill what you can and send back.

Based on similar customers, a strawman we often propose for a 20–80M token range is: committed slab pricing at $15–20 per 1M tokens with an ability to burst (pay-as-you-go) and a short-term burst buffer for TPS. If your peak TPS is >500 we typically suggest a dedicated capacity conversation.

Can you confirm the three items above? I can then spin a formal proposal and schedule a 30-minute follow-up to go over numbers.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Dylan: +1 (415) 555-0132
redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-hosted-pricing-worksheet.xlsx
From: Kira Mitchell <kira@atlashealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput & spend alignment — quick clarifying items

Thanks Dylan — appreciated the demo. Quick answers below and I've attached a short forecast for Q3 (atlas-forecast-q3.csv).

Answers:
- Monthly token volume: our initial pilot expects ~40–60M tokens/month. Longer term (12 months) the model could run 120–180M but that's post-pilot.
- TPS: steady-state average ~1.2 TPS for triage microservice; peak burst windows observed in internal stress tests up to 420 TPS sustained for ~3–6 minutes during morning intake surges. We also see short spikes up to ~700 TPS but only a handful per week (very short, ~10–20s).
- Budget target: leadership has given a ballpark of $18–22 per 1M tokens for hosted consumption during pilot. We need to keep pilot spend to <$1,200/month if possible (narrow constraint for pilot), then open to committed pricing for production.
- SLA/residency: must be US-only region; SOC2 evidence helpful but not strict blocker.

Question: how does Redwood count tokens for billing — is it prompt + completion or completion only? Also curious how burst TPS affects the committed slab (do we need a separate burst quota?).

-Kira
Kira Mitchell
Dir. of Product Operations, Atlas Health
kira@atlashealth.com
Attachment: atlas-forecast-q3.csv
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T10:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: throughput & spend alignment — quick clarifying items

Forwarding Kira's reply — key numbers: pilot 40–60M tokens/month, pilot budget target <$1.2k/mo, peak bursts ~420T/s sustained 3–6m, occasional micro-spikes to 700T/s. Must be US-only.

Quick ask for pricing + ops recommendation:
- Can we put together a pilot hosted proposal that meets the <$1.2k/month cap while still supporting the 420 TPS 3–6 minute bursts? If not, what committed slab and burst buffer would we recommend for a 50M/month baseline to hit leadership target ~$18/1M?
- Kira asked about token counting — default is prompt + completion; please confirm how this impacts sample monthly cost given their average completion length (~400 tokens) and prompt size (~80 tokens).

I'll leave it to you both to draft an approach. I'm proposing we offer a 60-day pilot slab (50M tokens) at a slightly discounted rate to hit their budget and include a temporary burst reserve to cover intake windows, then ramp to committed 100M slab if we see the higher trajectory.

-Dylan

> On 2027-05-25 09:18, Kira Mitchell wrote:
> > (quoted earlier email and attachment)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: throughput & spend alignment — quick clarifying items

Thanks — looked through Kira's numbers and their forecast. Suggested offer below (draft language for proposal):

Proposal (pilot -> production):
- Pilot: 60-day hosted pilot, committed slab = 50M tokens (prompt+completion billing).
  - Price: $17 per 1M tokens (pilot discounted rate).
  - Burst buffer: include free burst credit up to 500 TPS for aggregated 10 minutes/day (covers morning surges). Additional burst beyond buffer billed at pay-as-you-go $0.30 per 1k tokens consumed during burst window.
  - Pilot spend example: 50M * $17/1M = $850 (meets their <$1.2k constraint).

- Production (if they ramp): committed options at 100M tokens @ $15/1M or 200M tokens @ $12/1M with predictable monthly billing and SLA. Burst terms to be negotiated based on observed patterns in the pilot.

Token counting note: Redwood bills on prompt + completion token usage. For Atlas's numbers (avg prompt 80 + avg completion 400 = ~480 tokens per call):
- If steady-state 1.2 TPS = ~103.7k tokens/min ~6.22M tokens/day -> ~186M tokens/month (this is worst-case if every call sustained 1.2TPS 24/7; confirm their daily active hours).
- The numbers above show we should confirm active hours; the forecast CSV will help. If most traffic is concentrated, the pilot slab still makes sense but produce careful caveats about month-over-month variability.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Send the pilot proposal PDF (proposal-draft.pdf) to Kira with the 60-day 50M slab at $17/1M and burst buffer terms.
2) Schedule a 30-minute traffic pattern workshop with their engineering team to validate hourly distribution (we need to confirm sustained vs short spikes).
3) Collect SOC2 evidence and US region confirmation for the contract addendum.

I've attached a pricing-model-summary.xlsx with the cost math and a quick template for the pilot agreement. I'll draft the proposal doc and share a DocuSign link once you approve language.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: proposal-draft.pdf, pricing-model-summary.xlsx
